import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set up the figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis: 1000 Cameras Overview', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Color palette
palette = sns.color_palette("husl", n_colors=len(df['sensor_type'].unique()))

# 1. Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type (scatter plot)
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
for i, sensor in enumerate(df['sensor_type'].unique()):
    subset = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(subset['megapixels'], subset['price_usd'], alpha=0.6, 
                label=sensor, s=30, color=palette[i])
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', loc='upper left', fontsize=8)
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 2. Average Price by Brand (top 10 brands by count)
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
top_brands = df['brand'].value_counts().head(10).index
brand_prices = df[df['brand'].isin(top_brands)].groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=True)
colors = sns.color_palette("viridis", n_colors=len(brand_prices))
bars = ax2.barh(brand_prices.index, brand_prices.values, color=colors)
ax2.set_xlabel('Average Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Brand', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Average Price by Top 10 Brands', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')
# Add value labels
for bar, val in zip(bars, brand_prices.values):
    ax2.text(val + 50, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, f'${val:.0f}', 
             va='center', fontsize=9)

# 3. Camera Body Type Distribution with 4K capability
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
body_4k = df.groupby(['body_type', 'has_video_4k']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
body_4k.columns = ['No 4K', 'Has 4K']
body_4k.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=ax3, color=['#ff9999', '#66b3ff'], edgecolor='black')
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Number of Cameras', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Camera Body Type Distribution with 4K Video Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.legend(title='4K Video')
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
ax3.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')

# 4. Megapixels Evolution Over Model Years
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
yearly_stats = df.groupby('model_year')['megapixels'].agg(['mean', 'std']).reset_index()
ax4.fill_between(yearly_stats['model_year'], 
                 yearly_stats['mean'] - yearly_stats['std'],
                 yearly_stats['mean'] + yearly_stats['std'],
                 alpha=0.3, color='steelblue', label='±1 Std Dev')
ax4.plot(yearly_stats['model_year'], yearly_stats['mean'], 
         color='steelblue', linewidth=2.5, marker='o', markersize=6, label='Mean MP')
ax4.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Megapixels Evolution Over Time', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.legend(loc='upper left')
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
